title: Owandy Radiology to Debut AI Segmentation to QuickVision 3D Implant Planning Software at GNYDM
html:
Automatic separation of teeth, jawbones and canals helps clinicians review CBCT scans and plan guided implant surgery.

Owandy Radiology Inc., will introduce automatic AI Segmentation for QuickVision 3D, its advanced implant planning software, at booth #3614 during the Greater New York Dental Meeting (GNYDM), which opens on Sunday, November 29, and runs through December 1 at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center in New York. 

The new feature separates key anatomical structures on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans so clinicians can review the anatomy and move from scan review to surgical guide design within the same software.

In this manner, QuickVision 3D automatically separates the upper and lower jaws, individual teeth from crown to root, and anatomical canals, including the mandibular canal. 

Clinicians can now view each structure separately to assess available bone volume, examine root anatomy and locate structures they need to preserve when planning implant placement. Human clinical judgement is required to review and validate the AI-generated segmentation.

“When you’re planning an implant, you need to see how the proposed site relates to the available bone, nearby roots and the mandibular canal,” Boris 

Loyez, vice president of sales and marketing for Owandy Radiology North America, stated in a press release. “By separating those structures automatically, QuickVision 3D gives clinicians a head start on reviewing the scan. They can verify the anatomy and use that information to plan implant placement more accurately and design the surgical guide in the same workflow.”

QuickVision 3D is an open, feature-rich implant planning platform that enables clinicians to review panoramic and cross-sectional views, overlay digital impressions on CBCT data, and simulate implant placement using a library of implant models. With QuickVision 3D, clinicians can also design surgical guides and export them for 3D printing.

For endodontic planning, QuickVision 3D’s AI segmentation isolates individual teeth from crown to root on CBCT scans, helping clinicians examine root anatomy as they locate root canals, especially those that are not detectable by two-dimensional x-rays.

GNYDM attendees can visit Owandy Radiology at booth #3614 during the 3-day exhibition at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center in New York. For more information about QuickVision 3D and AI segmentation, visit owandy.com, call 516-858-5695 or email [email protected].

Headquartered in France, and serving North America from Garden City, New York, Owandy Radiology is a global leader in the manufacture of dental radiology hardware and imaging software designed for the most demanding dental professionals.
